entries.mistake: backtick inside a template literal (for example in a comment inside a CSS or HTML template)
entries.rule: escape the inner backtick
entries.guard: the missing delimiter could instead be a closing backtick
entries.note: an unescaped backtick inside a template literal

entries.mistake: top-level `await` in a script
entries.rule: wrap the code in an async function and call it, or run it as a module
entries.guard: wrapping changes the scope of every declaration and the completion value; a host may instead choose async-function-body mode for the whole call
entries.note: top-level await is the most frequent syntax-level mistake

entries.mistake: redeclared `let`/`const`/`class` at top level (often across repeated evaluations in one global scope)
entries.rule: rename, assign instead of redeclaring, or evaluate each call in a fresh scope
entries.guard: every fix changes meaning
entries.note: redeclaring let/const between evaluations in one global scope

entries.mistake: extra closing delimiter `)` `]` `}` after a complete expression or statement
entries.rule: delete the one closing token the parser reports as unexpected
entries.guard: apply only if (a) the token is a closer with no matching opener, (b) deleting it parses and the first error moves past it, and (c) no rival reading parses: inserting the matching opener at the start of the statement (for `)` only when the wrapping would change the meaning, since parenthesising a whole expression statement means the same thing; for `]` always) or, for `}`, where a body without braces could begin (after `)`, `else`, `=>`, `do`, `try`, `finally`); otherwise suggest
entries.note: extra closing delimiters are the one syntax mistake seen repeatedly; only some are fixed by deleting the reported token

entries.mistake: missing `)` / `]` / `}` in the middle of the source
entries.rule: insert the closer where the indentation or the next statement suggests
entries.guard: more than one position parses
entries.note: a missing closer in the middle of a call

entries.mistake: TypeScript type syntax in JavaScript: parameter/variable annotations, `as T`, `interface`/`type` declarations
entries.rule: erase the type syntax (annotations, `as` casts, interface and type-alias declarations); runtime meaning is unchanged
entries.guard: only for the erasable subset (no enum, valueful namespace, parameter properties, decorators); apply only if the erased source parses; the annotations of one parameter list and its return type are one repair, and a chain `x as A as B` is one repair; code that is meant to be TypeScript is out of scope
entries.note: type annotations appear in code meant for a plain JavaScript host

entries.mistake: closing brackets missing at the very end of the input (truncated output)
entries.rule: append the closers for the open-bracket stack, innermost first, at end of input
entries.guard: apply only if every parse error is at the end of the input (end of input inside open brackets, including a call or array cut off mid-list) and the stack is non-empty; never close an open string or template literal; indentation is evidence: if a later line is indented no deeper than the line of an open `{` and is not itself a closer, that `{` was left open in the middle of the file and nothing is applied; closers go innermost first, a `}` on its own line at the indentation of its opener's line, `)` and `]` directly after the last token

entries.mistake: markdown code fence lines around the program
entries.rule: remove lines that consist only of ``` or ```<language> at the start or end of the input
entries.guard: a fully fenced block already parses (the backticks form template literals), so this check runs before parsing: if the first or last non-blank line is only a fence, strip it; apply only if the result parses (when the source did not parse to begin with, the other rules may finish the job and the whole repair must parse)

entries.mistake: typographic quotes used as string delimiters
entries.rule: replace U+2018/U+2019 with ' and U+201C/U+201D with " when they open or close a string where the parser expects a token
entries.guard: only outside strings, comments, template literals and regular expressions ; apply only if the result parses; pairs must match (open/close)

entries.mistake: missing comma between elements, properties or arguments on separate lines
entries.rule: insert `,` after the previous element when the next line starts a new element
entries.guard: the innermost open bracket is `[`, the `(` of a call or the `{` of an object literal (not a block); the previous token ends a value and the next one, on a new line, starts a value or property; inserting there makes the first error move on

entries.mistake: Python keyword or operator in place of the JavaScript one: `elif`, `and`, `or`
entries.guard: only when the word is the reported unexpected identifier, sits where an operator or `else if` belongs, and the result parses; `not`, `def`, `in range`, `:` blocks, `None/True/False` are not mechanical (see S-PY)

entries.mistake: comma between class members
entries.rule: delete the comma
entries.guard: only directly between two class elements; result parses

entries.mistake: backslash before a quote outside a string (JSON-escaped code pasted raw)
entries.rule: remove the backslash
entries.guard: only when the lexer rejects a backslash that precedes a quote; every escaped quote from there to the end of that line is unescaped in one repair; apply only if the result parses

entries.mistake: HTML entities in code: `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`
entries.rule: decode the entity
entries.guard: only outside strings, comments and template text; every entity in code is decoded in one repair; apply only if the decoded source parses

entries.mistake: literal backslash-n between statements
entries.rule: replace the two characters `\n` with a line break
entries.guard: only outside strings, templates, regular expressions and comments, where `\` cannot start a token; every such `\n` is replaced in one repair; apply only if the result parses

entries.mistake: top-level `return`
entries.rule: put the code in a function, or end with the value as an expression
entries.guard: the intended result depends on the host

entries.mistake: unterminated string, or a literal line break inside a string
entries.rule: close the string, use `\n`, or use a template literal
entries.guard: the fix choice changes the string

entries.mistake: other Python-isms: `def`, `for x in range()`, f-strings, `None/True/False`
entries.rule: translate by hand
entries.guard: no mechanical rewrite keeps the meaning; `None/True/False` parse and fail at run time as undefined names

entries.mistake: `import`/`export` in a script
entries.rule: run as a module
entries.guard: module mode changes strictness and `this`

entries.mistake: `try` without `catch`/`finally`
entries.rule: add a catch clause
entries.guard: the handler body is the author's
